messages:
carlos (AE): Hey all — Orbitia asked for a short POC to validate swapping from VendorX to Redwood. Their checklist: prompt parity on 3 canonical flows, consistent tokenized responses, rate-limit behavior, and a security questionnaire. They also want pricing ballpark for a 6-month dedicated pool. Can ops + SEs drive the POC?
anya (SE): I can lead the prompt parity tests. Do we have their example prompts?
carlos (AE): Sent earlier via email but copying one here: `GetCustomerSummary(customer_id)` + follow-up clarifications. They said the competitor returns extra narrative text that clients rely on.
rachel (Solutions): We need to map the competitor's response schema — lots of customers have brittle parsing. Suggest we add an acceptance test that asserts a JSON path and max extra text length.
mike (Platform Eng): For latency SLAs they expect <120ms p50 for short chat queries. On our hosted tier we can hit that with the recommended model but Dedicated pricing varies depending on GPU class.
anya (SE): Quick note: we saw a consistent delta in tokenization for numeric lists. I'll run a small harness comparing VendorX model vs Redwood curated v1 on the 50 prompt set.
sam (Security): Orbitia requires KMS integration and proof of key separation for Dedicated. Also wants proof of no persistent KV caching of PII. I'll need the security questionnaire filled (I'll attach answers).
tessa (Legal): Also flag IP/data residency: they process EU customer PII and need data residency + DPA. We can offer Private deployment or Dedicated with EU region.
carlos (AE): Pricing ask: they want an estimate: 2M tokens/month plus peak concurrency 250 rps, ~3M tokens embedding usage. Can we give a committed monthly price for Dedicated?
mike (Platform Eng): Rough calc: for 250 rps sustained we'd recommend a 4-GPU pool (A100-equivalent) with burst autoscale. Ballpark commit for capacity (6mo) ~ $86k/month, plus network/storage. I'll get exact numbers from infra cost model.
rachel (Solutions): For the POC acceptance criteria propose: 1) JSON field parity for top-3 endpoints, 2) delta token inflation <8%, 3) p50/p95 latency within 20% of VendorX baseline, 4) no unexplained hallucination on a 100-example eval set.
carlos (AE): Orbitia legal also asked about log ingestion/telemetry — they want request IDs in logs and optional redaction of request content. Is that supported?
mike (Platform Eng): We emit request IDs and can redact payloads at rest for Dedicated/Private. For Hosted, we have stricter retention rules; we'll document exact retention windows.
anya (SE): I'll attach a simple curl harness to run locally against Redwood hosted and their VendorX endpoint for parity tests:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-curie-1","input":"Summarize customer 12345"}'
```
I will diff the outputs and surface schema/parse failures.
rachel (Solutions): Good. Also add a normalization shim for whitespace/newline tokens; often the competitor strips trailing bullets which breaks parsers.
sam (Security): For the questionnaire — two quick blockers: 1) Orbitia requires their own logging endpoint for audit copies (we can support via log-forwarding but need a contract addendum), 2) they require HSM-backed signing of logs for compliance. Both are doable but need Legal + SRE signoff.
tessa (Legal): I'll draft the addendum language for log-forwarding and HSM. Please send exact retention and dataflow diagrams.
mike (Platform Eng): SRE note: to mirror VendorX rate-limit semantics we can expose a compatibility header: `X-Rate-Limit-Policy: vendorx-compat` but we should warn customers about burst smoothing differences.
carlos (AE): Orbitia also asked about SDK/API surface parity — minor differences in error codes caused issues. Can we provide a compatibility guide?
anya (SE): Yes — I'll produce a short mapping table: VendorX error -> Redwood error + recommended handling.
deploy-bot: deployed rc/compat-shim v0.1 to staging at 1767124120
mike (Platform Eng): Staging shim live. Anyone able to run the initial 50-prompt parity run in staging?
anya (SE): Running now, will post failures in ~30m.
carlos (AE): Timeline for POC: kickoff today, parity run in 48h, security questionnaire answers + draft legal addendum in 72h, pricing proposal within 5 business days. Orbitia is on a tight timeline so let's keep tight SLAs here.
rachel (Solutions): Noted. I'll prepare the acceptance test harness and share a runbook.
sam (Security): I'll start the questionnaire. If Orbitia needs a SOC2 attestation, we have the report available — I'll attach summary.
anya (SE): Quick interim finding: first 10 prompts show VendorX appends an attribution line. We can strip or emulate based on a compatibility flag. Flagging as potential behavioral delta for the acceptance criteria.
carlos (AE): Perfect. Thanks team — I'll update Orbitia and share the next steps. If anything blocks, ping me @carlos. :thumbsup:
